prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 3 rows, 12 circles total. Regular equal square cells, landscape4:3 ratio for12circles or square for16circles. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. A few free electrons: Only three tiny electron motes suspended in abundant dark space. Avoid: Same electron marks as electrons, visibly fewer; not a new particle species.
2. Radiation escaping into space: A small warm diffuse patch at lower left sends three pale radiation strokes into a large empty upper field. Avoid: Energy leaves a body; no enclosing atmosphere and no cosmic expansion grid.
3. Molecular hydrogen: Two touching diffuse ivory atomic lobes around two small nuclear centres, an enlarged molecule schematic. Avoid: No orbit lines; same molecule as cloud-h2 despite its different formation route.
4. A knot that can cool: The same three-lobed gas knot with two faint radiation strokes leaving its edge. Avoid: Keep diffuse irregular outline; no dense central star yet.
5. A collapsing gas core: The same knot tightened into a compact bright centre with three inward tapering gas streams. Avoid: Converging gas remains dominant; avoid a finished stellar disk.
6. A massive protostar: A small warm luminous centre half-veiled by thick infalling gas, with two inward streamers. Avoid: Enveloped and actively accreting; massive first-star context has no solid dust.
7. A massive first star: A clean ivory stellar disk with feathered amber edge and long uneven rays, little surrounding gas. Avoid: Established exposed star, not a fireball or a dust-ringed Sun.
8. Starlight: An off-centre small ivory star sends a fan of long fine uneven rays into dark space. Avoid: Visible local stellar source; sunlight uses the established warmer young-Sun source.
9. Ionized surrounding gas: A diffuse gas patch with separated nuclear dots and tiny free electron motes, illuminated from one side. Avoid: A schematic ionized region, not a chemical dye or a second star.
10. A glowing nebula: A broad luminous scalloped gas veil surrounding a small off-centre star, feathered ivory edges. Avoid: Cloud emits a coherent glow; no solid dust or rich modern nebula colours.
11. Compression in the stellar core: A stellar cutaway with a compact central region and three short converging ivory pressure cues. Avoid: Slow contraction inside intact star; no exploding shell or collapsing void.
12. Hydrogen nuclei in the stellar core: A broad stellar cutaway enclosing a sparse enlarged field of simple proton beads in its luminous core. Avoid: Clearly inside the existing star, not hydrogen being added from outside.
